title: The Surviving Works of Tacitus
authorityNotice: Ancient Roman historical literature. It is included for historical study and is not presented as Scripture.
collectionNotice: The Annals survive in Books 1–6 and 11–16; Books 7–10 are lost, with additional lacunae in the surviving books. The Histories survive in Books 1–5 and break off during Book 5.

works.title: Agricola
works.purpose: To honor Tacitus’s father-in-law Agricola, recount his public career and campaigns in Britain, and reflect on virtuous leadership under oppressive rule.

works.title: Germania
works.purpose: To describe the lands, peoples, customs, and political life of the Germanic tribes for a Roman audience, often using them as a contrast with Roman society.

works.title: Dialogue on Oratory
works.estimatedDate: Probably c. 102 CE; both date and attribution remain debated
works.purpose: To explore why Roman public oratory seemed to have declined and to compare the claims of rhetoric, poetry, education, and political conditions.

works.title: Histories
works.purpose: To narrate Rome’s civil wars and imperial upheaval beginning in 69 CE and to examine how ambition, armies, and court politics shaped imperial power.

works.title: Annals
works.purpose: To trace imperial rule from the death of Augustus through the Julio-Claudian emperors, examining power, corruption, resistance, and the loss of republican freedom.
